title: Star Wars vs Star Trek
shortAnswer: Star Wars ($70B+ franchise) is the #3 highest-grossing franchise ever, known for epic space opera storytelling and The Force. Star Trek (since 1966) is more cerebral, explores social issues through science fiction, and has a dedicated 'Trekkie' fan base. Star Wars leads in box office; Star Trek leads in TV longevity.
verdict: Star Wars for epic cinematic spectacle and pop culture dominance. Star Trek for thought-provoking sci-fi and TV longevity. Both are pillars of science fiction.

lines.hook: One franchise is worth seven times the other. It still loses this fight.
lines.tape: Star Wars owns the box office. Star Trek owns the medium it was born in.
rounds: Seventy billion against ten. Star Wars isn't a franchise, it's an economy.
Five live action shows versus thirteen series. Trek never stopped making television.
Ten point three billion in ticket sales. Trek's films are a rounding error.
Trek got there eleven years earlier, and it did it on TV.
Trek built episodes around real arguments. Star Wars built a myth instead.
lines.verdict: Trek takes it three to two. Pick Star Wars if you want spectacle over sermon.

youtubeTitle: Star Wars vs Star Trek: The Numbers Pick a Winner
youtubeDescription:
Star Wars is a $70 billion franchise with $10.3 billion at the box office. Star Trek started in 1966 and has produced 13+ series built around real social commentary. We compare franchise value, TV output, box office, longevity and substance to settle which sci-fi giant actually wins.

Figures accurate as of October 2026. Statistics change over time — see the full, maintained comparison at https://www.aversusb.net/compare/star-wars-vs-star-trek
